problem: Express $\frac{2{x}^{2}+7x-1}{({x}^{2}-2x+3)(x+1)}$ as a sum of partial fractions.

feedback.problem: Express $\frac{3{x}^{2}-3x+1}{({x}^{2}+3)(x-2)}$ as a sum of partial fractions.
feedback.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A,$ $B,$ and $C$ such that

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}-3x+1}{({x}^{2}+3)(x-2)}=\frac{Ax+B}{({x}^{2}+3)}+\frac{C}{(x-2)}.
$$

Note that since ${x}^{2}+3$ is an irreducible quadratic factor, we must use a linear term $Ax+B$ in the numerator.

We multiply both sides by $({x}^{2}+3)(x-2)$ and get

$$
3{x}^{2}-3x+1=(Ax+B)(x-2)+C({x}^{2}+3).
$$

Plugging in $x=2$ eliminates $A$ and $B$ and allows us to solve for $C.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}3(2)^{2}-3(2)+1 & =(A(2)+B)(2-2)+C({2}^{2}+3) \\ 12-6+1 & =7C \\ C & =\frac{7}{7} \\ C & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Plugging in $x=0$ eliminates the $A$ term, and using our result for $C$ allows us to solve for $B.$ We get 

$$
\begin{aligned}3(0)^{2}-3(0)+1 & =(A(0)+B)(0-2)+C({0}^{2}+3) \\ 1 & =-2B+3C \\ 1 & =-2B+3(1) \\ 2B & =2 \\ B & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to solve for $A,$ we choose $x=1$ and use our results for $B$ and $C.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}3(1)^{2}-3(1)+1 & =(A(1)+B)(1-2)+C({1}^{2}+3) \\ 1 & =-A-B+4C \\ 1 & =-A-1+4(1) \\ A & =3-1 \\ A & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So we have $A=2,$ $B=1$ and $C=1.$ Therefore, our final result is

$$
\frac{3{x}^{2}-3x+1}{({x}^{2}+3)(x-2)}=\frac{2x+1}{({x}^{2}+3)}+\frac{1}{(x-2)}.
$$
